mainTopic: Whether נעילה exempts ערבית, טבילה בזמנה מצוה, the meaning of a קרי on יום הכיפורים, and the close of מסכת יומא.
overview: This last amud of מסכת יומא finishes the question of whether תפילת נעילה exempts a person from ערבית after יום הכיפורים. The גמרא answers that it is a dispute between תנאים, shown by when a בעל קרי may immerse on יום הכיפורים. A second ברייתא seems to flip רבי יוסי's view. The גמרא resolves this: one ruling is for someone who already davened נעילה, the other for someone who has not. This leads to the idea that the רבנן hold טבילה בזמנה מצוה, immersing on time is itself a מצוה. A ברייתא about ה׳'s name written on the skin seems to contradict רבי יוסי's view. The גמרא answers that the ruling against immersing after נעילה belongs to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who holds 'it is enough to immerse at the end.' The amud then explains the wording of a ברייתא about rubbing before immersion. It closes with אגדה teaching that a קרי on יום הכיפורים is a good sign: forgiveness, עולם הבא, long life and children. A הדרן ends the מסכת.

steps.title: Ending the challenge: הבדלה must be said in חונן הדעת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge from the previous דף: on מוצאי יום הכיפורים a person must daven a full ערבית because he needs to say הבדלה in חונן הדעת. This implies that נעילה does not exempt one from ערבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he must say הבדלה in the ברכה of 'חונן הדעת'!
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a challenge that began on the previous דף. The ברייתא requires a real ערבית after יום הכיפורים, because הבדלה is said inside the ברכה of חונן הדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person must daven ערבית in order to say הבדלה in חונן הדעת, then נעילה clearly did not exempt him from ערבית. This attacks the view that נעילה פוטרת של ערבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The declaration separating holy time from regular time, said when a holy day ends.
The fourth ברכה of the עמידה ('Who graciously grants knowledge'). On מוצאי שבת and יום טוב, אתה חוננתנו is added to it.
The fifth and final תפילה of יום הכיפורים.
The evening תפילה.

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not stand alone. It is the punchline of a challenge that started on the previous דף, so do not read it as the start of a new discussion.

phrases.english: because he must recite havdala
phrases.notes: The reason a full ערבית is needed after יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: in 'Who graciously grants knowledge'!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows that this line is the challenge itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹמַר הַבְדָּלָה בְּחוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that תפילת נעילה exempts one from ערבית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires a full ערבית after יום הכיפורים so that הבדלה can be said in חונן הדעת. That means ערבית is still required, so נעילה did not exempt it.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים: the general rules of immersion on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question is a מחלוקת תנאים, and it begins quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first states the general rule that people who need טבילה may immerse on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As it was taught in a ברייתא: All who are obligated to immerse may immerse in their normal way on יום הכיפורים. A נדה and a יולדת immerse in their normal way on the night of יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the challenge is not decisive, because תנאים themselves argue about this question. It then starts quoting the ברייתא that will show the dispute, setting up the key case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts that the earlier ברייתא holds נעילה does not exempt ערבית, but says another תנא disagrees. The opening rules of the ברייתא are background: a טבילה done for a מצוה is not the forbidden washing (רחיצה) of יום הכיפורים. A נדה and a יולדת immerse at night because that is when their טבילה time arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is a dispute between תנאים.' The question is an argument among the sages of the משנה era.
People who are required to immerse in a מקוה in order to become טהור.
In their normal way, just as on any other day.
A woman after her period, and a woman after childbirth.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tannaim.
As it was taught: all who are obligated in immersions
phrases.notes: Introduces the ברייתא that proves the dispute.

phrases.english: immerse in their usual way on Yom Kippur.
A menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth
immerse in their usual way on the night of Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: Their immersion time is at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by turning it into a recognized dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing as a dispute between תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier ברייתא seems to refute the view that נעילה exempts ערבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא represents only one side. Another תנא holds that נעילה does exempt ערבית, as the ברייתא being quoted will show.

steps.title: The בעל קרי case shows the dispute about נעילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a בעל קרי may immerse until מנחה, while רבי יוסי says he may immerse all day. This reveals two views on whether נעילה is a nighttime תפילה that exempts ערבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בעל קרי may immerse at any point until מנחה. רבי יוסי says: the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The two opinions on when a בעל קרי may immerse reflect two views of when נעילה is davened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under תקנת עזרא, a בעל קרי must immerse before davening. The תנא קמא says that after מנחה he should not immerse, but should wait for night, because נעילה is said at night and so counts as ערבית. רבי יוסי says he may immerse all day, because נעילה is said while it is still day and he needs to be טהור for it, which means it does not exempt ערבית.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission. Under the decree of עזרא, he must immerse before davening or learning תורה.
He may go on immersing, meaning he may immerse at any point.
Until the time of the afternoon תפילה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source the גמרא uses to show that whether נעילה exempts ערבית is a real מחלוקת between תנאים.

phrases.english: One who had a seminal emission may go on immersing
until the afternoon prayer.
phrases.notes: After that, he waits until night.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the entire day.
phrases.notes: He holds that נעילה is said during the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל קֶרִי — טוֹבֵל וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 2 and supplies the actual dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים disagree about whether נעילה exempts ערבית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a בעל קרי immersing on יום הכיפורים: the תנא קמא says until מנחה, and רבי יוסי says all day.

steps.title: A second ברייתא reports רבי יוסי's view the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites another ברייתא. In it, the תנא קמא says a בעל קרי immerses all day, while רבי יוסי says he cannot immerse from מנחה onward. This contradicts רבי יוסי's view in the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a contradiction was raised: The זב, the זבה, the male and female מצורע, one who had relations with a נדה, and one who is טמא מת all immerse in their normal way on יום הכיפורים. A נדה and a יולדת immerse in their normal way on the night of יום הכיפורים. A בעל קרי may immerse at any point the whole day. רבי יוסי says: from מנחה onward he cannot immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof by quoting a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says the opposite of what he said in the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, רבי יוסי allowed immersion all day. Here he forbids it from מנחה onward. If his opinion is unclear, it is hard to use him as one side of the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted them.' A formula that introduces a source contradicting the previous one.
A man or woman with an abnormal discharge that makes them טמא.
A person afflicted with צרעת.
A man who had relations with a נדה and became טמא.
A person who became טמא through contact with a dead body.

steps.confusionAlert: In this second ברייתא the two positions are swapped. The 'all day' view now belongs to the תנא קמא, and רבי יוסי holds the stricter view. Read carefully who says what.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: the zav and the zava
the male leper and the female leper
and one who had relations with a menstruating woman, and one impure from a corpse
immerse in their usual way on Yom Kippur.
A menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth
immerse in their usual way on the night of Yom Kippur.
One who had a seminal emission may go on immersing
the entire day.
Rabbi Yosei says:
from the afternoon prayer onward
he is not able to immerse.
phrases.notes: This contradicts רבי יוסי's view in the first ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 3 by showing a conflicting version of רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's position in the first ברייתא: that a בעל קרי may immerse all day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא has רבי יוסי forbidding immersion from מנחה onward, which is the exact opposite of his ruling in the first ברייתא.

steps.title: Resolution: did he already daven נעילה or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי יוסי forbids immersion when the person already davened נעילה, and he permits it when the person has not yet davened נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where he already davened תפילת נעילה. That ruling is where he did not daven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both statements of רבי יוסי are true, because each one refers to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person has not yet davened נעילה, he may immerse even late in the day so that he can daven it while it is still day. If he already davened נעילה, there is no need left, so he may not immerse after מנחה. רבי יוסי's view stays consistent: נעילה is a daytime תפילה, so the proof of the dispute between תנאים stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' A formula that introduces the resolution of a contradiction.
'This... that...' Each source is assigned to a different case.
He prayed (Aramaic).

steps.whatToRemember: Whether נעילה exempts ערבית is a dispute between תנאים. The first ברייתא shows it: the תנא קמא says a בעל קרי waits for night after מנחה, since נעילה is a nighttime תפילה. רבי יוסי lets him immerse all day so he can daven נעילה by day. רבי יוסי's opposite-sounding ruling in the second ברייתא refers only to someone who already davened נעילה.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he prayed the ne'ila prayer,
phrases.notes: This is the case of the second ברייתא, which says no immersion from מנחה onward.

phrases.english: that is where he did not pray.
phrases.notes: This is the case of the first ברייתא: he may immerse all day so he can daven נעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּצַלִּי תְּפִלַּת נְעִילָה, הָא דְּלָא צַלִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seems to contradict himself about immersing after מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי permits immersion before the person has davened נעילה and forbids it after he has. His view that נעילה is a daytime תפילה remains consistent.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן allow immersion after נעילה?
steps.stepSummary: If the person already davened נעילה, what is the reason the רבנן allow him to immerse all day?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he already davened, what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the רבנן's side. If he already davened נעילה, he has no more תפילות left that day, so why would the רבנן let him immerse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said a בעל קרי immerses so that he can daven. After נעילה he has nothing left to daven on יום הכיפורים. So the רבנן's permission to immerse all day seems to have no purpose, and we need to know their reason.

keyTerms.meaning: that he davened (here: he already davened נעילה)
what is their reason?
the Rabbis (the majority view, the תנא קמא)

phrases.english: If he had already davened (נעילה),
phrases.notes: Refers to the case from Step 5 where רבי יוסי forbids immersion.

phrases.english: what is the reason of the Rabbis (who allow immersion all day)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 5's split between before and after נעילה, and asks about the רבנן's side of the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן allow immersion even after נעילה, when no תפילה remains on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The רבנן hold that immersing on time is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה, so one immerses on time even with no תפילה left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, in the רבנן's view, immersing on time is a מצוה by itself. It does not need to be for the sake of davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose of the immersion is not only to prepare for תפילה. The immersion itself, done at the right time, is a מצוה. So even after נעילה the person should immerse.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold / they are of the opinion
immersion at its proper time is a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of טבילה בזמנה מצוה is the key concept for the rest of this sugya.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן hold טבילה בזמנה מצוה, so the immersion has value even with no תפילה left.

steps.title: A ברייתא about ה׳'s name written on the skin
steps.stepSummary: This implies רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה. The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא about someone who has ה׳'s name written on his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that רבי יוסי holds it is not a מצוה. But a ברייתא teaches: If ה׳'s name was written on a person's skin, he may not wash, may not smear oil, and may not stand in a dirty place. If a מצוה immersion came up for him, he wraps a reed around the name, goes down, and immerses. רבי יוסי says: he goes down and immerses normally, as long as he does not rub the spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference: if the רבנן hold טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה, then רבי יוסי must hold it is not. It then quotes a ברייתא that seems to show רבי יוסי holding the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the תנא קמא wants the name protected with a reed. רבי יוסי lets him immerse normally, even though the water touches the name. This sets up the challenge, which the next line completes by explaining what the two sides disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference / this implies
ה׳'s name
a reed / rush, wrapped as a covering
rub

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about יום הכיפורים or a בעל קרי at all. The גמרא uses it only to learn what רבי יוסי holds about טבילה בזמנה.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לָאו מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Yosei holds it is not a מצוה.
phrases.notes: Since he forbids immersion after נעילה.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה שֵׁם כָּתוּב עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ —
phrases.english: If ה׳'s name was written on his flesh —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִרְחַץ וְלֹא יָסוּךְ
phrases.english: he may not wash and may not smear oil (lest the name be erased)
and he may not stand in a filthy place (out of respect for the name).
If a מצוה immersion came up for him —
he wraps a reed over it, goes down, and immerses.
Rabbi Yosei says:
he goes down and immerses in his usual way
provided that he does not rub (the spot).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לָאו מִצְוָה. וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes Step 7's answer about the רבנן, infers the opposite view for רבי יוסי, and brings a source that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא of the written name, רבי יוסי lets the person immerse right away without a covering. This suggests he values immersing on time, which is the opposite of the inference.

steps.title: Their dispute is about immersing on time
steps.stepSummary: We know that the dispute in that ברייתא is about whether טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה, so רבי יוסי there holds it is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we maintain that they disagree about whether immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge. It states that the argument in the ברייתא is exactly about whether immersing on time is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds it is not a מצוה, so if he has no reed he should wait rather than risk erasing the name. רבי יוסי holds it is a מצוה, so he immerses now even without a covering. That clashes with what we inferred about רבי יוסי from יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: and we have established / we maintain
they disagree

phrases.english: And we maintain
that they disagree about whether immersion at its proper time is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: So the רבי יוסי of that ברייתא holds it IS a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַיְימָא לַן דְּבִטְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 8 by explaining the ברייתא in a way that makes the contradiction clear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inferred position of רבי יוסי (טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the written-name ברייתא is about טבילה בזמנה, then רבי יוסי holds it is a מצוה. He cannot hold both views.

steps.title: That רבי יוסי is a different person
steps.stepSummary: The רבי יוסי in the second יום הכיפורים ברייתא (who forbids immersion from מנחה onward, implying טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה) is really רבי יוסי בר יהודה. The plain רבי יוסי of the written-name ברייתא holds that it is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That (ברייתא) is רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבי יוסי of the יום הכיפורים ברייתא, who forbids immersion after מנחה, is actually רבי יוסי בר יהודה. He is a different תנא from the plain רבי יוסי of the written-name ברייתא, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference that רבי יוסי holds 'not a מצוה' came from the יום הכיפורים ברייתא, where he forbids immersing after נעילה. The גמרא says that ruling is really רבי יוסי בר יהודה's, and he holds טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה. The plain רבי יוסי, as shown in the written-name ברייתא, holds it is a מצוה. Two people with two views means no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: that one (that ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יוסי with רבי יוסי בר יהודה. They are different תנאים, and the whole answer depends on that difference.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא.
phrases.english: That (ברייתא) is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the יום הכיפורים ברייתא that forbids immersion from מנחה onward, the one we used to show he holds it's not a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 8–9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the opinion belongs to a different תנא with a similar name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות quote the same רבי יוסי, so his views contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יום הכיפורים ברייתא (no immersion from מנחה onward) quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who holds טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה. The plain רבי יוסי of the written-name ברייתא holds it is a מצוה, so the two sources do not clash.

steps.title: It is enough to immerse at the end
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה saying it is enough for the immersion to be at the end. This shows he holds that טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה, which fits the רבי יוסי of the יום הכיפורים ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: It is enough for the immersion to be at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי יוסי בר יהודה does not require immersing at the exact proper time. This supports naming him as the author of the יום הכיפורים ruling that forbids immersing after נעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a case of doubt about which day to immerse, one view requires immersing again and again so that one of the immersions falls on the right day. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says one immersion at the end, when it is surely valid, is enough. So in his view there is no מצוה to immerse at the proper time, exactly the view implied by the רבי יוסי who forbids immersion after נעילה on יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: it is enough for it
at the end

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן hold טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה, so a בעל קרי may immerse even after נעילה. The רבי יוסי of the יום הכיפורים ברייתא, who forbids it, is really רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who holds 'דיה לטבילה שתהא באחרונה': טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה. The plain רבי יוסי of the written-name ברייתא holds it is a מצוה, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
It is enough for the immersion to be at the end.
phrases.notes: Said about a case of doubt about which day is the right day to immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 10 by showing רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה.
steps.raayaObject: That the יום הכיפורים ruling (no immersion after נעילה, implying טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה) belongs to רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי בר יהודה says, 'It is enough for the immersion to be at the end.'

steps.title: A ברייתא about immersing after קרי on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who has a קרי on יום הכיפורים goes down and immerses, and 'rubs in the evening.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone who has an emission on יום הכיפורים goes down and immerses, and in the evening he should rub.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the topic of טבילה on יום הכיפורים. It also sets up a wording problem that the גמרא will raise next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that he immerses right away fits the view from earlier steps that immersing on time is a מצוה. The phrase 'in the evening he should rub' is unclear. Rubbing removes dirt or anything stuck to the skin, which counts as a חציצה that blocks the immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא
Goes down into the מקוה and immerses
He should rub his skin to remove anything blocking the water

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sees an emission on Yom Kippur
goes down and immerses,
and in the evening he should rub.
phrases.notes: This wording is what the גמרא will question next.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה קֶרִי בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ברייתא about טבילה on יום הכיפורים, continuing the theme of immersing on time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who has a קרי on יום הכיפורים immerses right away, and there is a rubbing requirement linked to 'evening.'

steps.title: Why rub after the immersion is already done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what good rubbing in the evening can do, since the immersion already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the evening? What happened, happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. Rubbing after the immersion cannot fix an immersion that is already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing is only useful before immersing, because it removes things that block the water. If he rubs that night, after he already immersed during the day, it cannot change whether the immersion counted.

keyTerms.meaning: What happened, happened; it is too late to change it

phrases.english: In the evening?
What was, was!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the phrase 'וְלָעֶרֶב יְשַׁפְשֵׁף' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'in the evening he should rub'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rubbing only helps before immersion, so rubbing afterward is pointless.

steps.title: Read it as rubbing the evening before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading to 'from the evening before he should rub,' and concludes this תנא holds that rubbing is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: from the evening before, he should rub. This תנא holds that rubbing is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. He rubs his body on ערב יום הכיפורים so he is ready in case he needs to immerse on יום הכיפורים itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing לָעֶרֶב to מִבָּעֶרֶב moves the rubbing before the immersion, so it makes sense again. The note 'קא סבר מצוה לשפשף' tells us this תנא treats preparing the body by rubbing as a real מצוה. That is why he does it ahead of time and not on יום הכיפורים, when washing is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; the גמרא corrects or rereads the text
From the evening before (ערב יום הכיפורים)
He holds; tells us the reasoning or view behind a ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The rubbing must come before the טבילה, so it is done on ערב יום הכיפורים, and this תנא holds it is a מצוה to rub.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
from the evening before, he should rub.
(He holds that it is a מצוה to rub.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by rereading the word 'evening.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rubbing happens on the night after יום הכיפורים, after the immersion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rubbing happens on ערב יום הכיפורים, before any immersion. Rubbing is a מצוה.

steps.title: A קרי on יום הכיפורים means his sins are forgiven
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב נחמן that one who has a קרי on יום הכיפורים has his sins forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: Someone who has an emission on יום הכיפורים, his sins are forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the הלכה of immersion to what this event says about the person spiritually. A ברייתא says it is a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new, more aggadic thread on the same case. The claim is that the emission does not show rejection. It is a sign that his sins are forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות taught in front of [a sage]
His sins are forgiven for him

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:
One who sees an emission on Yom Kippur,
his sins are forgiven for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same case (קרי on יום הכיפורים), but now about its spiritual meaning rather than the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרי on יום הכיפורים is a sign that one's sins are forgiven.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says his sins are 'lined up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא that says his sins are 'arranged,' which sounds bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: his sins are arranged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. Another ברייתא says this person's sins are 'lined up,' as if they are set out against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Arranged' sounds like his sins are laid out for judgment and punishment. That seems to be the opposite of 'forgiven.'

keyTerms.meaning: Arranged, lined up

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
his sins are arranged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the 'forgiven' ברייתא with a ברייתא that sounds negative.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Arranged' implies his sins are set out for judgment, which clashes with 'forgiven.'

steps.title: 'Lined up' means lined up to be forgiven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'arranged' means arranged in order to be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'arranged' mean? Arranged to be forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining the unclear word. The sins are lined up so they can be wiped away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות do not argue. 'Arranged' is not about punishment. It describes the sins being set out for forgiveness, so both sources give a positive message.

keyTerms.meaning: To be forgiven

phrases.english: What is 'arranged'?
Arranged to be forgiven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction by explaining the word סְדוּרִין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Arranged' means his sins are set out against him for judgment.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Arranged' means set out to be forgiven, which matches 'forgiven.'

steps.title: Worry all year, but surviving it guarantees עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that he should worry all year, and if he survives the year he is assured of עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Someone who has an emission on יום הכיפורים should worry the entire year. If he makes it through the year, he is promised that he has a share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא with a mixed message. It could be a bad sign, but if he lives through the year, it turns out to be a very good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the emission shows his fast was rejected. Surviving the year shows the opposite: his good deeds protected him, and he is guaranteed עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
He should worry
The year passed for him safely; he survived the year
One who has a share in the World to Come

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
One who sees an emission on Yom Kippur
should worry the entire year,
and if the year passes for him,
he is assured
that he has a share in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another view on what a קרי on יום הכיפורים means, with an uncertain start and a positive outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worry all year. Surviving the year assures him a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows why it is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק supports the positive outcome: everyone else is 'hungry' while he is 'satisfied.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: You can know this, because the whole world is hungry and he is satisfied.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a reason that supports the good reading of the ברייתא. On יום הכיפורים everyone holds back from marital relations, but this person's desire was calmed without any sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the emission happened by itself and was not done on purpose, it is like שמים 'feeding' him while others go hungry. That kindness from Heaven shows he has merit.

keyTerms.meaning: Know [that it is so]; introduces a supporting proof
Hungry; here, longing because of holding back from relations
Satisfied

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Know it,
for the whole world is hungry
and he is satisfied.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תֵּדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the positive ending of רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרי on יום הכיפורים can be a sign of Heavenly favor
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning that he was 'satisfied' while everyone else was 'hungry'

steps.title: רב דימי: a sign of long life and children
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, arriving from ארץ ישראל, says it is a sign that the person will live long, grow, and raise offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: He will have a long life, he will grow, and he will cause others to grow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings the teaching of ארץ ישראל, which is fully positive. This emission is a sign of long life and many descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מְפֵישׁ חַיֵּי means he will live long, and סָגֵי וּמַסְגֵּי means he will grow and raise others, like children. Some link this to the פסוק 'יִרְאֶה זֶרַע יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים' (ישעיהו נג:י): 'seeing seed' goes together with long days.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came [from ארץ ישראל to בבל]
Increases life; lives long
Grows and makes others grow (has children)

steps.whatToRemember: The final word on a קרי on יום הכיפורים is positive: forgiveness, עולם הבא, long life, and offspring.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
he will lengthen his life,
grow, and cause others to grow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fully positive tradition from ארץ ישראל, ending the aggadic thread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרי on יום הכיפורים is a sign of long life and offspring.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק יום הכיפורים and מסכת יומא
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the last פרק, יום הכיפורים, and the end of מסכת יומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק יום הכיפורים, and מסכת יומא is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional הדרן line that marks the end of the פרק and of the whole מסכת. No new argument is made here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses the learner's promise to come back to this material. Here it closes both the eighth פרק and מסכת יומא as a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing formula for a פרק
And it is completed
The tractate dealing with יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] Yom HaKippurim,
and Tractate Yoma is concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing after the final aggadic teaching.
